summary: A history of libertarian attempts to found tax-free floating nations, from the 1971 Republic of Minerva near Tonga through New Utopia, the Freedom Ship and the Seasteading Institute to the failed 2021 crypto cruise ship Satoshi, most of them grifts.

evidence.note: Michael Oliver founds the Republic of Minerva on a reef off Tonga in 1971; earliest narrated project
Tonga's king uses the military to seize the reef in June 1971
Turney gets rich selling growth hormone, later pitches unapproved anti-aging drugs for New Utopia
SEC labels New Utopia a fraudulent internet scheme
Norman Nixon's Freedom Ship project begins its long fundraising run
Seasteading Institute founded 2008 by Patri Friedman with Peter Thiel money
2017 memorandum with French Polynesia; long segment on its collapse amid local protest
host frames the French Polynesia plan as exploiting a climate-threatened island territory
Thai navy declares the Elwartowski seastead a threat to sovereignty in April 2019
Satoshi cruise ship venture in Panama collapses and the ship is sold for scrap

notes: No theme for libertarianism, micronations or tax havens; fraud-grift chosen as primary since the host frames most projects as grifts, but Elwartowski and Ocean Builders are presented as sincere. Sealand and Heinlein are brief context, so covered_span starts at Minerva 1971. Turney birth year inferred from death in 2012 at 88. Republic of Minerva left to keywords for lack of subject slots.
